THIS MFA IS FILED UNDER SECTION 173(1) OF MV ACT AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 08.02.2017 PASSED IN MVC NO. 24/2015 ON THE FILE OF XXL ADDL. SCJ AND XIX ACMM MEMBER - MACT, BANGALORE, PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FURTHER HEARING,
THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

In this appeal, the petitioners have challenged the judgment and award dated 08.02.2017 passed in M.V.C.No.24/2015 on the file of the XXI Additional Small Causes Judge and M.A.C.T. (SCCH-23),
Bengaluru (for short 'the Tribunal'), dismissing the claim petition.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Briefly stated the facts are, husband of petitioner No.1, father of petitioners Nos.2 and 3, one Prabhu @ Ashok @ Prabanna, the deceased, on NC: 2023:KHC:28715 02.12.2014 at about 5.40 p.m., on M.S.Palya Main Road, M.S.Palya, Bengaluru, was a pillion rider in motor cycle bearing No.KA-02/HZ-4535, met with an accident as the rider hit against the motor cycle to an electrical pole, injuring the deceased.

He was treated at NIMHANS, Bengaluru and then at Victoria Hospital,
ultimately on 07.12.2014, the deceased died.
The petitioners being the dependants have approached the Tribunal seeking compensation.
Claim was opposed by the Insurance Company.
After taking evidence, the Tribunal passed the impugned judgment dismissing the claim petition.
Aggrieved by the same, the petitioners have filed this appeal on various grounds.

4. Heard Smt.M.R.Shalamala, learned counsel for the petitioners and Sri.Ravi S.Samprathi, learned counsel for the insurer.
5.
It is the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioners that charge sheet filed against the NC: 2023:KHC:28715 rider of the motor cycle has not been challenged by anybody.

Soon after the accident, the deceased was taken to Nagappa Hadli Hospital and thereafter directly to NIMHANS,
Bengaluru.
The deceased was never taken to K.C.General Hospital.
Ex. R2
relied upon by the Insurance Company has nothing to do with the deceased, so also the accident in question.

There is no material to show that the accident was due to self-fall, the Tribunal wrongly relied upon Ex.R2 in Smt. Shruthi vs Shivaswamy on 11 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99772629/
2 dismissing the claim petition and sought for re-consideration and assessment of the compensation.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 6. Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company has contended that Ex.R2 is the trump card, which is also marked as Ex.R8 where it is mentioned that the deceased was brought to K.C.General Hospital with a history of 'self-fall from two-wheeler on 02.12.2014 at 6.30 p.m. near M.S.Palya'.
This aspect has been suppressed by the NC: 2023:KHC:28715 petitioners; five days after the accident, complaint was lodged.
Even the Investigating Officer i.e., RW- 1/R.Mohan Kumar, the Police Inspector has hand in glove with the petitioners.

The Tribunal has rightly rejected the claim petition as the same is filed only for the sake of compensation and he supported the impugned judgment.
7.
I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments advanced on behalf of both parties and perused the materials on record.
8. The entire records did point out two versions i.e., deceased was taken to Nagappa Hadli Hospital with a history of 'R.T.A.' and then he was sent to higher hospital.
According to the petitioners, the deceased was not at all taken to K.C.General Hospital, he was directly taken to NIMHANS.

According to the Insurance Company, the deceased was taken to K.C.General Hospital at 12.50 p.m.
and because of suspected head injury, he was referred to NC: 2023:KHC:28715 surgery and therefore, the deceased was taken to NIMHANS with a history of accident.
Dr.Nirmala is the Casualty Medical Officer of K.C.General Hospital.

Ex.R2 refers that on 2.12.2014 at 6.30 p.m., the deceased was brought to K.C.General Hospital by one Ramesh, during that time, the deceased was not conscious and the history is furnished as 'self-fall from two-wheeler'.
It is pertinent to note that two days after the accident, the deceased was taken to NIMHANS, but no records pertaining to NIMHANS has been placed before the Tribunal.
9. Now the issue is, whether the deceased was taken to K.C.General Hospital from Nagappa Hadli Hospital or he was taken from Nagappa Hadli Hospital to NIMHANS directly?
In this regard, there is no evidence at all and the petitioners are not bothered to rebut Ex.R2, document relied upon by the Insurance Company.
If the argument of the petitioners is to be believed, the only issue before NC: 2023:KHC:28715 this court is, whether the deceased was treated at K.C.General Hospital or not.
In this regard, matter requires re-consideration and unless is it ascertained that whether the deceased was brought to K.C.General Hospital or directly taken to NIMHANS from Nagappa Hadli hospital.
If it is established that the deceased was taken to K.C.General Hospital, there is no substance in the claim of the petitioners.

Since the petitioners have lost their only bread- earner and the claim under Section 166 of the M.V.Act being under a beneficial legislation, it is a fit case for remand for fresh consideration rather dismissing it.

In the result, the following:
ORDER i) The appeal is allowed.
ii) The impugned judgment is set aside.

3 iii)

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The matter is restored to the file of Tribunal to the stage of evidence.

The petitioners to secure the relevant witnesses from K.C.General hospital as NC:
2023:KHC:28715 well as NIMHANS, to ascertain whether the deceased was treated at K.C.General Hospital, Bengaluru, on 02.12.2014 at 6.30 p.m. or he was directly taken to NIMHANS and to decide the case afresh in accordance with law, without being influenced by any of the observations made hereinabove.
iv) Without further notice, the parties shall appear before the Tribunal on 28th August, 2023.
v) The amount in deposit, if any, shall be returned to the Insurance Company.

Sd/-
